entries.proposition: Design: double-blind placebo-controlled parallel-group phase 3 in 65 sites, 1:1:1 randomisation to two fenfluramine groups and placebo after a 4-week prospective baseline, 14 weeks of treatment.
entries.snippet: After a 4-week baseline to establish baseline seizure frequency, patients were randomized 1:1:1

entries.proposition: Concomitant antiseizure medications, diet and stimulator settings could not change during the trial, which removes one confounder of a seizure count.
entries.snippet: Changes in antiseizure medications, dietary therapy, and vagus nerve stimulation settings were not permitted during the trial.

entries.proposition: Primary endpoint is the percentage change in expert-panel-confirmed drop-seizure count versus placebo, a count; key secondaries include 50 percent responder rate and a clinician-rated global improvement scale.
entries.snippet: The primary end point was the percentage change from baseline in Epilepsy Study Consortium–confirmed drop seizures

entries.proposition: Multiplicity was controlled by a serial gatekeeping hierarchy; nominal P values below a failed gate are explicitly not significance.
entries.snippet: End points were assessed for statistical significance only if all end points that were higher in the hierarchy were significant at the α = .05 level.

entries.proposition: Sample size assumed a 30 percent or greater mean decrease against placebo and 50 percent SD.
entries.snippet: assuming an estimated mean decrease of 30% or greater in drop seizures for fenfluramine vs placebo and assuming 50% SD and 20% attrition

entries.proposition: Primary result: the higher-dose group had an estimated median difference from placebo of minus 19.9 percentage points (interval minus 31.0 to minus 8.7, P .001); the placebo group itself fell by a median 7.6 percentage points.
entries.snippet: Patients who received 0.7 mg/kg/d of fenfluramine achieved an estimated median difference from placebo of −19.9 percentage points (95% CI, −31.0 to −8.7 percentage points; P = .001)

entries.proposition: The lower-dose group difference was minus 10.5 (interval minus 25.0 to 4.0, P .09), an interval that includes zero and is not a null.
entries.snippet: In the 0.2-mg/kg/d fenfluramine group, the estimated median difference from placebo was −10.5 (95% CI, −25.0 to 4.0 percentage points; P = .09)

entries.proposition: Maintenance-period sentence: at the 25 percent or greater responder level, 46 of 87 patients (54 percent) on the higher dose, 41 of 89 (47 percent) on the lower dose and 29 of 87 (33 percent) on placebo achieved a reduction in drop seizure frequency; this sentence follows the maintenance-period 50-percent results and is not the titration-plus-maintenance figure (the next entry).
entries.snippet: At the 25% or greater responder level, 46 of 87 patients (54%) in the 0.7-mg/kg/d fenfluramine group (P = .009), 41 of 89 patients (47%) in the 0.2-mg/kg/d fenfluramine group (P = .10), and 29 of 87 (33%) in the placebo group achieved reduction in drop seizure frequency.

contradicts_locator.what_changed: Proposition narrowed after the blind audit (OVERSHOOT). Was: Responders (50 percent or more): 22 of 87 on the higher dose and 9 of 87 on placebo; at the 25 percent level, 29 of 87 (33 percent) improved on placebo. The original mixed periods: it gave the 50-percent figures of the titration-plus-maintenance period (22 of 87, 9 of 87) beside the maintenance-period 25-percent placebo figure (29 of 87). The quoted snippet, anchor and artefact are unchanged unless stated.

audit.method: Blind audit of triples against the sources; persisted in disease-models/wwox/research/page_adjudications/locator_audit_R4b_R2b_20261022.md (commit ae343793). The repair itself is unaudited (blind audit OWED).

entries.proposition: Global impression: a clinically meaningful (much or very much) rating was given to 26 percent of the higher-dose group and 6 percent of placebo by investigators, 34 and 5 percent by caregivers; the any-improvement threshold separated the groups much less (49 versus 34 percent by investigators, P .06).
entries.snippet: The percentages of patients who were rated by investigators as having any improvement on the CGI-I scale were 49% (39 of 80 patients) in the 0.7-mg/kg/d fenfluramine group (P = .06), 45% (38 of 85 patients) in the 0.2-mg/kg/d fenfluramine group (P = .16), and 34% (27 of 80 patients) in the placebo group

entries.proposition: Generalised tonic-clonic seizures (present in 46 percent) fell by 45.7 percent on the higher dose against a 3.7 percent increase on placebo, a nominal subgroup result.
entries.snippet: compared with an increase of 3.7% (n = 38) in the placebo group

entries.proposition: Baseline imbalance: median drop-seizure frequency per 28 days was 83 and 85 in the fenfluramine groups against 53 in the placebo group.
entries.snippet: The median (range) frequency was higher in the 0.7-mg/kg/d and 0.2-mg/kg/d fenfluramine groups than in the placebo group (83 [7-1803] and 85 [4-2943] vs 53 [2-1761] events per 28 days, respectively).

entries.proposition: No valvular heart disease or pulmonary hypertension was observed in the 14-week trial, with echocardiography at baseline, maintenance and end of trial.
entries.snippet: No cases of valvular heart disease or pulmonary arterial hypertension were observed at any time.

entries.proposition: The authors name short duration as the one limitation; no developmental or adaptive endpoint was measured, and the executive-function claim is cited to other work.
entries.snippet: A limitation of this study is its short duration.

entries.proposition: Fig 2A: median reduction in drop seizures about 26 on the higher dose, about 14 on the lower dose and about 7 on placebo over titration plus maintenance; panel C: clinically meaningful improvement about 26 and 20 against 6 percent by investigators and about 34 and 27 against 5 percent by caregivers.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 2 panels A-D: A median percentage reduction titration+maintenance 26 / 14 / 7.6 (P .001, .09) and maintenance-only about 27 / 18 / 7 (P .002, .08); B responder bars at >=25, >=50, >=75; C rated improvement from baseline, any improvement investigator 49/45/34, caregiver 61/44/37, clinically meaningful investigator 26/20/6, caregiver 34/27/5; D countable motor seizures 26 / 12 / 8.

entries.proposition: Fig 3: in generalised tonic-clonic seizures the placebo bar is below zero (an increase) while both fenfluramine bars are 45 to 60 percent reductions; in atonic seizures the placebo reduction (about 28 percent) exceeds the lower-dose reduction (about 4 percent).
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 3 panels A (combined) and B (maintenance only) bars by seizure type: GTC higher dose about 46, lower dose about 58, placebo about -4; tonic about 31, 21, 13; atonic about 34, 4, 28; tonic or atonic about 47, 14, 7; maintenance panel GTC 53, 62, -3; atonic 52, 12, 34.

entries.proposition: Fig 1: 335 screened, 72 excluded (32 for cardiovascular or cerebrovascular history), 263 randomised, 242 completed; 247 continued to the open-label extension.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 1 CONSORT: 335 screened, 72 excluded, 263 randomized 87/89/87, withdrew 10/7/4, completed 242, continued to OLE 247 (78/83/86).

entries.proposition: Titration-plus-maintenance period: 50-percent or greater responders were 22 of 87 (25 percent) on the higher dose and 9 of 87 (10 percent) on placebo; at the 25 percent level the placebo group had 27 of 87 (31 percent) in that period.
entries.snippet: A greater proportion of patients in the 0.7-mg/kg/d fenfluramine group (22 of 87 [25%]; P = .02) and the 0.2-mg/kg/d fenfluramine group (25 of 89 [28%]; P = .005) experienced a 50% or greater reduction in drop seizure frequency compared with patients in the placebo group (9 of 87 [10%])

entries.proposition: The titration-plus-maintenance 25-percent responder placebo figure is 27 of 87 (31 percent), against 29 of 87 (33 percent) in the maintenance-only sentence.
entries.snippet: More patients in the active treatment groups achieved a 25% or greater reduction in drop seizures compared with placebo (27 of 87 [31%]) during the titration and maintenance period.

entries.proposition: NOT WWOX EVIDENCE (fenfluramine in Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, phase 3). The protocol cover page lists Amendment 3.0 (8 June 2020), Amendment 2.1 (29 July 2019), Amendment 1.0 for the rest of the world (10 January 2018) and the original protocol version 1.1 (13 July 2017).
entries.snippet: Date and Version of 08 June 2020 (Amendment 3.0) Study Protocol: 29 July 2019 (Amendment 2.1) 10 January 2018 (Amendment 1.0 ROW) 13 July 2017 Version 1.1 (Original Protocol)

entries.proposition: Amendment 3.0 removed the Vineland scale as a study assessment in Part 2 because, in the version programmed for electronic administration, the caregiver was presented with fewer questions than required to determine standard scores.
entries.snippet: Removal of VABS as a study assessment in Part 2; due to an error in the version programmed for electronic administration, the subject/caregiver was presented with fewer questions than required to determine standard scores.
entries.anchor: Protocol Appendix 11, summary of Amendment 3.0, item 1

entries.proposition: The protocol's primary efficacy endpoint for Part 1 is the percent change in drop-seizure frequency per 28 days between the combined titration and maintenance periods and baseline.
entries.snippet: The primary efficacy endpoint for Part 1 is the percent change in frequency of seizures that result in drops (DSF: drop seizure frequency) per 28 days between the combined Titration and Maintenance (T+M) and Baseline periods in Cohort A.

entries.proposition: The protocol states that the sample size for Part 1 Cohort A was estimated under the assumption that adding the drug at 0.8 mg/kg/day to current therapy leads to a mean decrease in drop seizures 30 percentage points greater than placebo.
entries.snippet: The sample size for Part 1 Cohort A was estimated under the assumption that adding ZX008 at 0.8 mg/kg/day to current therapy will lead to a mean decrease in drop seizures that is 30 percentage points greater than adding placebo to current therapy.

entries.proposition: The protocol's statistics section defines the second hierarchy CGI-I endpoint as the proportion rated by the investigator as minimally, much or very much improved.
entries.snippet: The second key secondary endpoint – the proportion of subjects assessed by the Principal Investigator as minimally, much, or very much improved on the CGI-I – will be analyzed using a Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test (CMH) stratified by weight strata.

entries.proposition: The protocol synopsis lists the proportion of subjects who achieve a clinically meaningful improvement, defined as much or very much improved, on the Clinical Global Impression of Improvement as assessed by the principal investigator.
entries.snippet: Proportion of subjects who achieve clinically-meaningful improvement (much or very much improved) in the Clinical Global Impression – Improvement as assessed by Principal Investigator comparing the ZX008 0.8 mg/kg/day and 0.2 mg/kg/day groups independently

entries.proposition: The gatekeeping table row for the global-impression step reads 'rating, as assessed by the principal investigator – Any' (the word 'Improvement' follows on the next line; the comparison with the synopsis and statistics definitions is carried by the other entries).
entries.snippet: rating, as assessed by the principal investigator – Any

entries.proposition: The protocol says a complete description of the statistical analyses will be available in a statistical analysis plan that will be finalized before the database is locked.
entries.snippet: A complete description of the statistical analyses and methods will be available in a SAP, which will be finalized before the database is locked.

entries.proposition: The protocol states that the drug was administered orally twice daily as an oral solution of fenfluramine hydrochloride containing 2.2 mg/mL fenfluramine.
entries.snippet: Fenfluramine was administered orally twice daily as an oral solution of fenfluramine hydrochloride containing 2.2 mg/mL fenfluramine.

entries.proposition: The protocol lists trace or greater mitral or aortic valve regurgitation in subjects aged 18 or under among its listed abnormalities.
entries.snippet: a. Trace or greater mitral or aortic valve regurgitation in subjects ≤18 years of age

entries.proposition: The protocol states that all subjects are required to have follow-ups at 3 and 6 months.
entries.snippet: All subjects are required to have follow-ups at 3 and 6 months.

entries.proposition: The protocol states that the mean and median percent change in drop-seizure frequency will be presented and its statistical significance assessed with a Wilcoxon signed-rank test.
entries.snippet: Both the mean and median percent change in DSF will be presented and the statistical significance of the percent change will be assessed using a Wilcoxon signed-rank test.

entries.proposition: The protocol's data-sharing text says written requests for data by legitimate investigators, researchers or clinicians may be submitted to the sponsor.
entries.snippet: Written requests for data by legitimate investigators/researchers/clinicians may be submitted to Zogenix, Inc.

entries.proposition: PANEL READING, eFigure 2A (page 3): in the combined titration and maintenance period the median difference from placebo in generalised tonic-clonic seizures is about -50 for the higher dose and about -60 for the lower dose (both P below .001, 38 patients per active arm and 38 on placebo), with overlapping intervals; the lower-dose point estimate (about -60) is the larger reduction against placebo than the higher-dose one (about -50) on this seizure type, while for drop seizures the lower dose is -10.5 (95% CI -25.0 to 4.0, P .146) and the higher -19.9 (-31.0 to -8.7, P .001); tonic seizures at the higher dose are -16.9 (-34.1 to 0.4, P .060).
